        <section class="content article-content mb-6" itemprop="articleBody">
          <p>The <a href="#h_01KJG46SGVDXEFEZPR6DQ0GW4R">Salesforce Customer Relationship Management (CRM) connector tools</a> let marketing and sales teams integrate with Salesforce from Optimizely Opal. The tools streamline workflows, from automating personalized content for new leads and suggesting relevant materials for sales follow-ups. They also provide actionable insights through dynamic reporting and proactive alerts for at-risk opportunities. Opal transforms how teams leverage their CRM for enhanced engagement, efficiency, and competitive advantage.</p><p>First, an Opal <a href="/hc/en-us/articles/36359944449805" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">administrator</a> must <a href="#h_01KJGAMXBZ63R87Z5P4WGBPA41">connect Salesforce CRM to Opal</a> using Optimizely Connect Platform (OCP). After installing the connector in OCP, individual Opal <a href="/hc/en-us/articles/4413199966221" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">users</a> and <a href="/hc/en-us/articles/43183109095949" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">agent builders</a> can <a href="#h_01KK01N9S5K4RP4WJ8DZQ43TJD">log in to Salesforce</a> to access their information from Opal. Administrators only need to install the Salesforce connection in OCP once.</p><h2 id="h_01KJGAMXBZ63R87Z5P4WGBPA41">Connect Opal with Salesforce<a class="link-anchor" href="#h_01KJGAMXBZ63R87Z5P4WGBPA41"></a></h2><p>The following video and steps walk you through connecting Opal with Salesforce CRM.</p><figure class="wysiwyg-media"><div data-oembed-url="https://optimizely.wistia.com/medias/as34973uqh"><iframe src="//fast.wistia.com/embed/iframe/as34973uqh" frameborder="0" allowfullscreen="" allow="encrypted-media" style="width: 100%; aspect-ratio: 16 / 9;"></iframe></div></figure><h3 id="h_01KK00M1RP73PGNMVH4MTC2QJR">Install Salesforce CRM in OCP<a class="link-anchor" href="#h_01KK00M1RP73PGNMVH4MTC2QJR"></a></h3><p>In the OCP <strong>App Directory</strong>, complete the following:</p><ol>
<li data-list-item-id="ea139bed19b9e2524fd80112f781f2073">Click the <strong>Opal Tool Salesforce CRM</strong> connector tool.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e814be4a990c39c83a7d1729057392a4e">
<p>Click <strong>Install App</strong>.</p>
<figure class="wysiwyg-image"><img style="aspect-ratio: 1800/1180;" src="/hc/article_attachments/44054252527117" alt="Screenshot of OCP App Directory showing the Install App button for the Opal Tool Salesforce CRM connector" width="1800" height="1180" class="img-enlargable"></figure>
</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e23dcc3ca31621d4b52511ccb60e1d5fb">Click the <strong>Settings</strong> tab</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ea0a1decb1dfc4a60780ac0ccec85c05b">Leave the <strong>Instance level Opal Oauth</strong> toggle off if you are using Optimizely managed Oauth.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e193cdebc90b38e38bebab6862af98a28">Enter your <strong>Salesforce instance URL</strong>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e396d4e5038c8301b633a23a240232c2a">
<p>Click <strong>Save</strong>.</p>
<figure class="wysiwyg-image"><img style="aspect-ratio: 800/417;" src="/hc/article_attachments/44054252528269" alt="Screenshot of the OCP Settings tab for the Salesforce CRM connector showing the Salesforce instance URL field and Save button" width="800" height="417" class="img-enlargable"></figure>
</li>
</ol><h3 id="h_01KKMB6NH5VW9AE3042WC5X1YR">Enable your toolset preferences<a class="link-anchor" href="#h_01KKMB6NH5VW9AE3042WC5X1YR"></a></h3><ol>
<li data-list-item-id="e902a86c65c04e7eeaec68dfb1d098c91">Expand the <strong>Tool Permissions</strong> section.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e0478ef989b3f49f41309f0ced6887f1a">
<p>Toggle the permissions on that you want.</p>
<ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e9aa02c1441d72620e727eaa64919d403">
<strong>Enable Data Reading </strong>– Tools that let Opal read data (list, get, describe, count objects, and reports) from Salesforce.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e2a4a2127eef87fdabf23c17ece2ea025">
<p data-renderer-start-pos="501"><strong>Enable Data Modification</strong> – Tools that let Opal update (create and update objects) in Salesforce.</p>
<figure class="wysiwyg-image"><img style="aspect-ratio: 1360/616;" src="/hc/article_attachments/44054294127501" alt="Screenshot of the Tool Permissions section in OCP showing the Enable Data Reading and Enable Data Modification toggles" width="1360" height="616" class="img-enlargable"></figure>
</li>
</ul>
<p>You can modify specific tool access within Opal.</p>
</li>
</ol><h3 id="h_01KKMB6VJVKDJXFNKJDJ57MWYA">Add the Salesforce CRM tools to your Opal instances<a class="link-anchor" href="#h_01KKMB6VJVKDJXFNKJDJ57MWYA"></a></h3><ol>
<li data-list-item-id="ed9b8e5e84a6f6f07ba304bf1fe47fd65">Expand the<strong> Add to Opal</strong> section.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="eae61be40fcbe3c00c0bef09543430d70">
<p>Click <strong>Add to Opal</strong> to register the Salesforce CRM connector tools to the corresponding Opal instance. Click <strong>Remove from Opal </strong>to remove the connection.</p>

Choose the tool that matches the operation you need to perform.</p><details><summary><code>salesforce_crm_count_object</code> – Counts records in any Salesforce object without retrieving the actual data.</summary><div><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e7c1df426d6a73379e9870bb172c84a70">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="ef175f523532f28b73a3de93cf3b490c2">When you want to know the total count of objects without seeing the actual data.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e3712771594bb825856ccb6f11adfaf39">To check if records exist before performing operations.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e9be68596028e7a1d8aee5fe29ab0d1d2">To verify data volumes efficiently.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e1c11ffc1cbef9237b8a1aedad1d1a909">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e156f7a5b4804d4c4199a7855fc298529">
<code>objectType</code> – Salesforce object type to count. For example, "Account", "Lead", or "Product_Catalog__c".</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e423c1c97cb626cac0eaf2be7b1dd6bf8">(Optional) <code>filters</code> – Filter conditions as JSON string. For example, '{"Industry": "Technology"}'.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="edad9dc67dbc8a43aff9caed8f1c500ec">(Optional) <code>createdAfter</code> – Filter records created on or after this date in YYYY-MM-DD format.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e48af3c8ff7941f9833baffe022333810">(Optional) <code>createdBefore</code> – Filter records created on or before this date in YYYY-MM-DD format.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e6ca2ec3d1d445fa7868694ac3308476a">(Optional) <code>customDateField</code> – Date or datetime field name to filter on, for instance "CloseDate".</li>
<li data-list-item-id="efe265fe5fad62499e44d3ec6334f853f">(Optional) <code>customDateAfter</code> – Filter records where <code>customDateField</code> is on or after this date in YYYY-MM-DD format.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e8c3625f541a3fcd0b8db90169093341f">(Optional) <code>customDateBefore</code> – Filter records where <code>customDateField</code> is on or before this date in YYYY-MM-DD format.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="ef49bf6d23a751eaab7ba2f7b65bb7da2">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="ee98918e2aa39de0b26d0118caab50cb5"><em>How many accounts are there in Salesforce?</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e237be6107aa3b11966bd57601054c547"><em>Count the number of leads created this month.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e1de9f6d1fe2a937e71ddec7beffd684f"><em>How many opportunities are closing this quarter?</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e6cd39c6722b6d0c74137d0ec04dd0754"><em>Count cases that were closed last week.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e364363b3aa670700df6ad6d616bbd256"><em>How many active products are in the Product Catalog?</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></div></details><details><summary><code>salesforce_crm_create_object</code> – Creates a new record in any Salesforce object.</summary><div><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e10e8e2c92094fc1e448c81c71decf15f">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="ec63183778a04ef91ec4d97a9df9efd0f">To create new records in Salesforce, such as Accounts, Leads, Contacts, Opportunities, or custom objects.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e5b4f68969328d2257100496764e28350">When you need to add data to Salesforce programmatically.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e4d2b5a372efbdd4a8e8995a950d77e01">To streamline the creation of standard or custom Salesforce records.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e91788fda0358b9adeea596cbbe900184">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e8829af687b172bd7d386b73a375f4058">
<code>objectType</code> – Salesforce object type to create a record in. For example, "Account", "Lead", or "Product_Catalog__c".</li>
<li data-list-item-id="eaa1c291fdf2c65a87aae26e9e16e328c">
<code>fields</code> – Field values as a JSON string. For example, '{"Name": "Acme Corporation", "Industry": "Technology"}'.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e1349c4382482fb302dbd97526487287f">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="ef7447c1dc2341a764592bf8eb0ab7316"><em>Create a new Account named "Global Innovations" with Industry "Technology".</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="ee4f6c2b73b7e225c3660ffdf35268fd7"><em>I need to create a Lead for Jane Doe, company "Example Corp", email "jane.doe@example.com".</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e509535de3d2026d74f15ff6e822cddf1"><em>Create an Opportunity named "Q2 2026 Expansion" with Stage "Prospecting" and CloseDate "2026-06-30".</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="ee62a8e407e2c53d0af1b9c131f7c0f0c"><em>Add a new product to the Product Catalog with Name "Super Widget", SKU "SW-001", and Price 29.99.</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></div></details><details><summary><code>salesforce_crm_describe_object</code> – Describes a Salesforce object and gets its field metadata.</summary><div><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="ebd1b7fed7618cc59abc0e7d92042ec6a">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e96d272eb85ff7ff415de5c527fcdb700">To discover available fields for an object before creating or updating records.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ed5d86c2c80951aa44f2abe09e46bc2c8">To check which fields are required, createable, or updateable.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e45e2644f124a33c92f374e165e743c16">To get valid picklist values for picklist fields.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e9ebd33f8e29e3e6540604090ab3460de">To understand field types and their data formats.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e31e1567f38a32e132825b5e833b68586">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul><li data-list-item-id="ed7b1146e7b611bea4a643eaf7803068e">
<code>objectType</code> – Salesforce object type to describe. For example, "Account", "Lead", "Product_Catalog__c".</li></ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e55787f920428b9f311f3cc2ac8136304">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="efacba18f5482ad4307246d4e039e2211"><em>Describe the Account object in Salesforce.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="ecd1d8cf6ff2e633abcca0ce51b3dec93"><em>Show me the fields available for the Lead object.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="eef0d1879e3a1ea5fb94048208bad8ed2"><em>What are the metadata details for the custom object Product_Catalog__c?</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></div></details><details><summary><code>salesforce_crm_get_object</code> – Retrieves a single record from any Salesforce object by ID or field search.</summary><div><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="ec6ca9d90ba4c2bc222b4b83d36e49ab8">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e0d965524bfbd4ddee6f15922c85b85f3">To fetch details of a specific Salesforce record when you know its ID.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ec9fe190ddebec09bd5036ce08e328930">To find a record by a unique field value, such as an email address or a custom SKU.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e710cf1524e2f1adaa6c12292312eee91">To retrieve information about a single Account, Lead, Contact, Opportunity, or custom object record.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="ebd6100037bd81755d50cdcb31c8ed0b3">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e04039be466259dd1603944259e261492">
<code>objectType</code> – Salesforce object type to query. For example, "Account", "Lead", "Product_Catalog__c".</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e17172cd65be59c342a8191d69beda0ad">(Optional) <code>recordId</code> – Salesforce record ID (18-character ID). If provided, <code>searchField</code> and <code>searchValue</code> are ignored.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e90390a35f4890d7a2e97b1a85b7b33fd">(Optional) <code>searchField</code> – Field name to search by, for instance, "Name", "Email", "SKU__c". Required if <code>recordId</code> is not provided.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e71766ea2ae9fd9343724426008524c01">(Optional) <code>searchValue</code> – Value to search for in the specified field. For example, "Acme"or "john@example.com". Required if <code>recordId</code> is not provided.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ef56037e15ddd9257e38a804c5f115837">(Optional) <code>fields</code> – Comma-separated list of specific field names to retrieve. For example, "Name,Email,Phone". If not specified, Opal returns all queryable fields.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e262e178111fcee4138fb62aa357a10b9">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e8f6b8bfa359f82a9329ff38095553451"><em>Get the account details for ID "0015e000001ABC123".</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e1892e2373a5161e05f20474ef7742c29"><em>Find the lead with email "john@example.com".</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e3c5c72ced1a1d9380c112fe324aef65b"><em>Retrieve the opportunity named "Q1 Deal".</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="eb94eab7c2b2a70cc0d4e7539f577b96f"><em>Show me the product details for SKU "PROD-12345".</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></div></details><details><summary><code>salesforce_crm_list_object</code> – Lists records from any Salesforce object with optional filtering, sorting, and pagination.</summary><div><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e94aa801451213bc9eadc9130ce6e0877">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e6f2b123e70ee01af35a1295f458abb93">To search and retrieve multiple records from standard or custom Salesforce objects.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e74985491171d671046fef6ed6959ae27">To filter records by any field using advanced operators.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="efa366d14c3d64e390e1c671fa945115e">To sort records by any field, including Amount, Name, CloseDate, or custom fields.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="eaa56ae438369911da9d5c29b754f3ada">To paginate through large result sets of Salesforce records.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e9c1c913a79fd246e97ce186f5d12148c">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e4ba951c6fedd1022c5891cc95a45f2f2">
<code>objectType</code> – Salesforce object type to query (for example, "Account", "Lead", "Opportunity").</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e1307baf08033f81c82ffb188e4381211">
<code>fields</code> – Comma-separated list of specific field names to retrieve (for example, "Name,Email,Phone").</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ec57964350e9c327d6beefd7c1efc0c30">(Optional) <code>filters</code> – Filter conditions as a JSON string.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="eda106ca13190a3ca04fe68bad6611fc9">(Optional) <code>createdAfter</code> – Filter records created on or after this date in YYYY-MM-DD format.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e0879c7d3f0fe6628833e6e702bb3eabd">(Optional) <code>createdBefore</code> – Filter records created on or before this date in YYYY-MM-DD format.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e065b1477a24cafe6006da3881f296b5f">(Optional) <code>customDateField</code> – Date or datetime field name to filter on. For example, "CloseDate".</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e383e804637288908eacd3e8666470fbd">(Optional) <code>customDateAfter</code> – Filter records where <code>customDateField</code> is on or after this date in YYYY-MM-DD format.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ef34d38fc262b50bbd0e184f5aa422fcf">(Optional) <code>customDateBefore</code> – Filter records where <code>customDateField</code> is on or before this date in YYYY-MM-DD format.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ee5bcf63801d077e0eadb8fd8177ec438">(Optional) <code>sortBy</code> – Field name to sort results by. For example, "Amount" or "Name".</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e2a98f168afddb17ff910d098d8addff6">(Optional) <code>sortOrder</code> – Sort order for results, "ASC" or "DESC".</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e8e548a08a5d846b31005e7eec013a8c7">(Optional) <code>limit</code> – Maximum number of results to return. Default, 100.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e609d0adf1eefcadb6ddb0fa582bcb6d4">(Optional) <code>nextRecordsUrl</code> – Salesforce pagination URL from previous response.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="eaef42283ab024f8af45559c72140edd5">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e06a8484766d601043253a78a236a6b8b"><em>List all accounts in the Technology industry, showing their Name, Industry, and Website.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e0f0eb4d1202cab32601b43f48561986b"><em>Show me the top five opportunities by amount, including their Name, StageName, and Amount.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e3e09ee8d6c9be7dae59fd230d20edcfc"><em>List leads created this month, displaying their Name, Email, and Company.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e9738accb0dbc39c5633c913abea6d921"><em>Find all cases with a "High" priority, showing CaseNumber, Subject, and Status.</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></div></details><details><summary><code>salesforce_crm_update_object</code> – Updates an existing record in any Salesforce object.</summary><div><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e188e7e10feab84c54c767c82ad396e83">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e0222fadb2bbed465951b18fbf152a3ff">To modify existing records in Salesforce, such as updating an Account's industry or a Lead's status.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e54a5012d61d1e2a05b2a930a19c7d3ce">When you need to change specific fields of a Salesforce record.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e301a71a27f11980a1fb3068e41b53d8e">To automate updates to records based on new information or workflow changes.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e4c29ad57da53ac40c805e08e3853a050">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e40a438f12cc111928ef649e5a1c9be19">
<code>objectType</code> – Salesforce object type to update. For example, "Account", "Lead", "Product_Catalog__c".</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e922aca43e69ac9944fbd0db1e126ab63">
<code>recordId</code> – The ID of the record to update.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e140e3fe5146986a41d5bc618666c48ad">
<code>fields</code> – Field values to update as a JSON string. For example, '{"Industry": "Finance", "Phone": "555-9876"}'.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e4f0cf4c509b97f290236320bd666c592">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="eef3a31aff17f57315bc436354523dc5b"><em>Update the Account with ID "0015e000001ABC123" to have Industry "Finance" and Phone "555-9876".</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e5e0e3bf73ca0ebac1c7c8734af9aa709"><em>Change the status of Lead "00Q5e000001XYZ789" to "Qualified".</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e65d7f55de6beb15aa5ca8a3ee0dc5822"><em>For Opportunity "0065e000001DEF456", set the StageName to "Closed Won" and Amount to 150000.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="ee4c02787c778610fb0d4a03d60809d6a"><em>Update the Price__c of Product_Catalog__c record "a005e000001ABC123" to 129.99.</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></div></details><h3 id="h_01KJG549ENYJSDB3VN1D4RA0PP">Custom objects<a class="link-anchor" href="#h_01KJG549ENYJSDB3VN1D4RA0PP"></a></h3><p>Custom objects are data structures your organization has added to Salesforce beyond the standard set. Use these tools to discover which custom objects exist in your org and to query or filter records within them.</p><details><summary><code>salesforce_crm_list_custom_object_records</code> – Lists records from Salesforce custom objects with optional filtering and pagination.</summary><div><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e46e3a74e8ff4882eb6ffd6ea387fa16d">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e6bbfc482273aa4138f4eaa1d69115c8e">To search and retrieve multiple records from any Salesforce custom object.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="eede319adaabfd8e7b94fe8cc6a71a21b">To filter custom object records by specific criteria, such as status or category.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e3c119fee0c968d1b1e0756f0573f920e">To sort custom object records by any field, including custom date or formula fields.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e6edfb64cedbcc1fb46b1426a7ff9bebe">To paginate through large sets of custom object records.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="eec9d34db24c00f7d405e249ea1f680a4">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="ef70fc11fc48aa2821e666ef398c9cd83">
<code>objectName</code> – Custom object API name. Must end with <code>__c</code>. For example, "Product_Catalog__c".</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e8d4a878e2b0495972fdbdccad62c48b0">(Optional) <code>filters</code> – Filter conditions as a JSON string.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e385bd38e9d5d4b0366519860c6f5ae6c">(Optional) <code>createdAfter</code> – Filter records created on or after this date in YYYY-MM-DD format.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e0dd1e62db9dffb1660e551d003bb19eb">(Optional) <code>createdBefore</code> – Filter records created on or before this date in YYYY-MM-DD format.</li>

<li data-list-item-id="ed1d81b47bac6d8c27324ef7e87b166cf">(Optional) <code>sortBy</code> – Field name to sort results by. For example, "Name" or "Price__c".</li>

</li>
</ul></div></details><h3 id="h_01KJG54MX5KJ5PWKH9VSWC3WB9">Reports<a class="link-anchor" href="#h_01KJG54MX5KJ5PWKH9VSWC3WB9"></a></h3><p>Use these tools to find, inspect, and run existing Salesforce reports. Start with the <code>salesforce_crm_list_reports</code> tool to discover available reports. Use the <code>salesforce_crm_describe_report</code> tool to review a report's structure and available filters before running it. Then use the <code>salesforce_crm_run_report</code> tool to retrieve the data.</p><details><summary><code>salesforce_crm_describe_report</code> – Retrieves metadata about a Salesforce report without executing it.</summary><div><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e416fb5b58de61bc5c032175bf1c85080">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="ed1299f335406a5b20a2700d333fb0f8a">Understand report structure before running it.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="edb8b55b6ee55c384eb76432411c761b4">See available columns and fields.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e40261a09b750c98e06cd12b1f6c2500b">Identify the filters you can apply.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e9a743899e61eeb7b111924e4b308a4af">Understand groupings and aggregations.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="eaa94ad2e29f48032b14ffa409d584781">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul><li data-list-item-id="ec2c1a0797627afcea4fc6c145b91c83b">
<code>reportId</code> – Salesforce report ID to describe. Starts with "00O". For example, "00O5e000001ABC123". Use the <code>salesforce_crm_list_reports</code> tool to find available report IDs.</li></ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="ed42112408b87b247f564ec89143730ba">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="efc8e9809cfece5f8d65ccfb99bde263d"><em>Tell me about Salesforce report "00O5e000001ABC123".</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e12a024d881fabc04dc5071433adf3d77"><em>What are the available columns and fields for Salesforce report "00O5e000001ABC123".</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></div></details><details><summary><code>salesforce_crm_list_reports</code> – Retrieves a list of all reports accessible to you.</summary><div><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e7e30c9fd79bfae35f1fdc3c5f42468b8">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="ec83b0e073eb5add832e2c90e9cf7f643">Discover available reports.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ef37f7e40089fe4aaed6aef705d84ccfe">Find reports by name or folder.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ea0d3455203dcdf9a22f055abbcb4b7b2">Identify report IDs for running or describing reports .</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="eda48d993296f82e6c7193a0451d2f486">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul><li data-list-item-id="e48ea5afaeae4f9e12eeb5fc5ac56d8f9">(Optional) <code>folderId</code> – ID to filter reports. Folder IDs start with "00l". For example, "00l5e000000ABC123".<ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e85f05bf4303618d066428c93105282cc">If provided, Opal returns only reports in this folder.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ef5b30ecdea8aff4a9bc909ab94ba317d">If not provided, Opal returns all accessible reports.</li>
</ul>
</li></ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="eb5a866b685e60049f65b0808fc4e8a46">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e1b3c7f5ba08a85b884ed66f515db2283"><em>List all reports.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="ec0f79e742e0a498820301d9f5cc39258"><em>List reports in a folderId: 00l5e000000ABC123<strong>.</strong></em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></div></details><details><summary><code>salesforce_crm_run_report</code> – Runs a Salesforce report and returns the data.</summary><div><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e42f62427c583973b68cba6e291bfa937">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e26acaa244bbe786d16ea66a59cfdcd7e">Execute an existing Salesforce report.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="effc3e37ddb518a178f3f1c9a2b03b5d9">Get report data with optional runtime filters.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ef344ff803e9748d181220ac2742da1f1">Retrieve aggregated and grouped data.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e2f95cec838e34681adc6e33528b1b112">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e1ec10a85f7ba10e7f62d4b723a367382">
<code>reportId</code> – Salesforce report ID to execute. Starts with "00O". For example, "00O5e000001ABC123". Use the <code>salesforce_crm_list_reports</code> tool to find available report IDs.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e71111f723a7d29c1f3d04bd9a3c186f2">(Optional) <code>filters</code> – Filter conditions as a JSON string.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e97017ba3a278c823698bce416d9ffe48">(Optional) <code>includeDetails</code> – Whether to include detailed report results in the response. Default, true. Set to false for faster execution when you only need metadata.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="ea53daf6cf9ad959b6976d69cd0b93648">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>

<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e9ba2c9815d604e9ba0d758307048b4a4"><em>Run a report with runtime filters: { "reportId": "00O5e000001ABC123", "filters": "{\"reportFilters\": [{\"column\": \"CLOSE_DATE\", \"operator\": \"greaterThan\", ' + '\"value\": \"2025-01-01\"}]}" }</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="ec4638ff2a43a831ae9a4af4eb45a0d45"><em>Run report without detailed results: { "reportId": "00O5e000001ABC123", "includeDetails": false } </em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></div></details><h2 id="h_01KJG9V3D0BTTH780QCC1A2GZJ">Use cases<a class="link-anchor" href="#h_01KJG9V3D0BTTH780QCC1A2GZJ"></a></h2><h3 id="h_01KJG9X3RF684XQ0M8KDJXWTMD">Personalize content for new leads<a class="link-anchor" href="#h_01KJG9X3RF684XQ0M8KDJXWTMD"></a></h3><p><strong>Challenge</strong> – Marketing teams struggle to create and deliver personalized content to new leads, leading to generic outreach and lower engagement.</p><p><strong>Solution with Opal</strong> – Opal can monitor Salesforce for newly created leads. Upon identifying a new lead, Opal automatically retrieves relevant details such as industry, company size, and expressed interests. Leveraging this data, Opal then drafts personalized marketing content, like a tailored email or a blog post summary, ready for review and immediate deployment by the marketing team. This ensures every new lead receives content that resonates, boosting engagement and qualification rates.</p><h3 id="h_01KJGA043Z96XYKDJ19M5M96X9">Automate content suggestion for sales follow-up<a class="link-anchor" href="#h_01KJGA043Z96XYKDJ19M5M96X9"></a></h3><p><strong>Challenge</strong> – Sales representatives spend time searching for appropriate content (case studies, product sheets, or demos) to share with prospects at different stages of the sales cycle, often leading to delays and inconsistent messaging.</p><p><strong>Solution with Opal</strong> – As opportunities advance through Salesforce stages, Opal proactively identifies the need for follow-up content. Based on the opportunity's details (for example, industry, specific product interest, or identified pain points), Opal searches your Content Marketing Platform (CMP) for the most relevant assets. It then suggests these assets directly to the sales rep or even drafts a personalized email incorporating the content, streamlining the follow-up process and ensuring timely, relevant communication.</p><h3 id="h_01KJGA0DJMCMKW4GW5ATY6JR0Z">Streamline opportunity reporting<a class="link-anchor" href="#h_01KJGA0DJMCMKW4GW5ATY6JR0Z"></a></h3><p><strong>Challenge</strong> – Business users need quick, up-to-date insights into sales pipeline health and opportunity status, but compiling reports from Salesforce can be time-consuming and require specific expertise.</p><p><strong>Solution with Opal</strong> – Ask Opal for a summary of open opportunities, top deals, or opportunities by stage. Opal queries Salesforce in real-time, aggregates the data, and presents it in an easily digestible format, such as a dynamic table or chart within an Opal canvas. This eliminates manual reporting efforts, providing instant, actionable insights for sales leaders and executives, unifying reporting into a single, accessible interface.</p><h3 id="h_01KJGA0TQ46DVDCVJPZPWQTA30">Proactive engagement for at-risk opportunities<a class="link-anchor" href="#h_01KJGA0TQ46DVDCVJPZPWQTA30"></a></h3><p><strong>Challenge</strong> – Sales teams often react to at-risk opportunities rather than proactively addressing potential issues, leading to lost deals. Identifying these opportunities early and knowing the best course of action is critical.</p><p><strong>Solution with Opal</strong> – Opal continuously monitors Salesforce opportunities for signs of risk, such as prolonged inactivity, approaching close dates without recent engagement, or changes in competitor presence. When an at-risk opportunity is detected, Opal alerts the sales representative and suggests next-best actions. This could include drafting a re-engagement email, recommending a specific piece of content to share, or prompting a call with a key stakeholder, letting you proactively intervene to keep deals on track.</p><h3 id="h_01KJGA14177VE19FEX0GQCE4SE">Competitive intelligence for sales pitches<a class="link-anchor" href="#h_01KJGA14177VE19FEX0GQCE4SE"></a></h3><p><strong>Challenge</strong> – Sales representatives need quick access to up-to-date competitive intelligence to effectively position Optimizely's solutions during critical sales pitches, but this information is often scattered or difficult to retrieve on demand.</p><p><strong>Solution with Opal</strong> – When a sales rep is preparing for a pitch, they can ask Opal for competitive intelligence related to a specific opportunity. Opal retrieves any competitor information stored in Salesforce for that opportunity and then leverages its extensive internal knowledge base (including up-to-date competitor analysis) to provide key differentiators, battle cards, and strategic talking points against the identified competitors. This empowers sales teams with instant, relevant insights to strengthen their pitches and close more deals.</p><div class="note"><p>If you use Opti ID, administrators can turn off generative AI in the Opti ID Admin Center. See <a href="/hc/en-us/articles/36402464751501" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Turn generative AI off across Optimizely applications</a>.</p></div>

          <%= partial('partial-article-list-sections', {
            id: 'section-' + section.id,
            parentId: '#' + id,
            sections: section.sections,
            activeCategoryId: activeCategoryId,
            activeSectionId: activeSectionId,
            activeArticleId: activeArticleId,
            partial: partial

          <% if (section.articles.length) { %>
            <ul class="list-none font-size-md pl-0 mb-0 collapse" :class="{ 'is-visible': isOpen }" id="section-<%= section.id %>" data-parent="#<%= id %>">

                  </a>
                </li>
              <% }); %>
            </ul>
          <% } %>

        </li>
      <% }); %>
    </ul>
  <% } %>
</template>

BodyMarkdown:
Salesforce CRM connector tools – Support Help Center                   

[Skip to main content](#page-container)

The [Salesforce Customer Relationship Management (CRM) connector tools](#h_01KJG46SGVDXEFEZPR6DQ0GW4R) let marketing and sales teams integrate with Salesforce from Optimizely Opal. The tools streamline workflows, from automating personalized content for new leads and suggesting relevant materials for sales follow-ups. They also provide actionable insights through dynamic reporting and proactive alerts for at-risk opportunities. Opal transforms how teams leverage their CRM for enhanced engagement, efficiency, and competitive advantage.

First, an Opal [administrator](/hc/en-us/articles/36359944449805) must [connect Salesforce CRM to Opal](#h_01KJGAMXBZ63R87Z5P4WGBPA41) using Optimizely Connect Platform (OCP). After installing the connector in OCP, individual Opal [users](/hc/en-us/articles/4413199966221) and [agent builders](/hc/en-us/articles/43183109095949) can [log in to Salesforce](#h_01KK01N9S5K4RP4WJ8DZQ43TJD) to access their information from Opal. Administrators only need to install the Salesforce connection in OCP once.

## Connect Opal with Salesforce[](#h_01KJGAMXBZ63R87Z5P4WGBPA41)

The following video and steps walk you through connecting Opal with Salesforce CRM.

### Install Salesforce CRM in OCP[](#h_01KK00M1RP73PGNMVH4MTC2QJR)

In the OCP **App Directory**, complete the following:

1.  Click the **Opal Tool Salesforce CRM** connector tool.
2.  Click **Install App**.
    
    ![Screenshot of OCP App Directory showing the Install App button for the Opal Tool Salesforce CRM connector](/hc/article_attachments/44054252527117)
    
3.  Click the **Settings** tab
4.  Leave the **Instance level Opal Oauth** toggle off if you are using Optimizely managed Oauth.
5.  Enter your **Salesforce instance URL**.
6.  Click **Save**.
    
    ![Screenshot of the OCP Settings tab for the Salesforce CRM connector showing the Salesforce instance URL field and Save button](/hc/article_attachments/44054252528269)
    

### Enable your toolset preferences[](#h_01KKMB6NH5VW9AE3042WC5X1YR)

1.  Expand the **Tool Permissions** section.
2.  Toggle the permissions on that you want.
    
    *   **Enable Data Reading** – Tools that let Opal read data (list, get, describe, count objects, and reports) from Salesforce.
    *   **Enable Data Modification** – Tools that let Opal update (create and update objects) in Salesforce.
        
        ![Screenshot of the Tool Permissions section in OCP showing the Enable Data Reading and Enable Data Modification toggles](/hc/article_attachments/44054294127501)
        
    
    You can modify specific tool access within Opal.
    

### Add the Salesforce CRM tools to your Opal instances[](#h_01KKMB6VJVKDJXFNKJDJ57MWYA)

1.  Expand the **Add to Opal** section.
2.  Click **Add to Opal** to register the Salesforce CRM connector tools to the corresponding Opal instance. Click **Remove from Opal** to remove the connection.
    
    ![Screenshot of the Add to Opal section in OCP showing the Add to Opal and Remove from Opal buttons for the Salesforce CRM connector](/hc/article_attachments/44178876909965)
    

After you complete the steps in this section, Opal users can then follow the steps in the [Authenticate with Salesforce CRM](#h_01KK01N9S5K4RP4WJ8DZQ43TJD) section.

### Configure the Salesforce CRM connector[](#h_01KKWB2DPKW1XARFM8RS01KPNA)

After an Opal administrator [adds the Salesforce CRM tools to your Opal instances](#h_01KKMB6VJVKDJXFNKJDJ57MWYA), a Salesforce Admin must complete the following steps in Opal:

1.  Go to **Tools > Connectors**.
2.  Click **Connect** on the **Salesforce CRM** connector.

This makes the Opal app available in Salesforce.

Open a new tab and go to Salesforce. Log in and complete the following steps once:

1.  Go to **Setup > Apps > Connected Apps > Connected Apps OAuth Usage**. See [Manage Current OAuth Connected App Sessions in the Salesforce documentation](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=xcloud.connected_app_manage_current_sessions.htm&type=5).
    1.  Click **Manage App Policies** on the **Opal** app. See [Manage Access to a Connected App in the Salesforce documentation](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=xcloud.connected_app_manage.htm&type=5).
    2.  Click **Edit policies** and adjust IP restrictions to **Relax IP restrictions**. See [Connected App IP Relaxation and Continuous IP Enforcement in the Salesforce documentation](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=xcloud.connected_app_continuous_ip.htm&type=5).
    3.  Click **Save**.
2.  Click **Install** on the **Connected Apps OAuth Usage** page.

## Authenticate with Salesforce CRM[](#h_01KK01N9S5K4RP4WJ8DZQ43TJD)

After an administrator [connects Opal with Salesforce CRM](#h_01KJGAMXBZ63R87Z5P4WGBPA41), log in from Opal to access your information. The Salesforce CRM connector tools use user-level authorization, so each Opal user can only access data they have permission to access in Salesforce.

To authenticate, complete the following steps in Opal:

1.  Go to **Tools > Connectors**.
2.  Click **Connect** on the **Salesforce CRM** connector tools.
    
    ![Screenshot of the Connectors page in Opal showing the Connect button on the Salesforce CRM connector](/hc/article_attachments/44051235968269)
    
3.  Log in to **Salesforce** in the window that Optimizely displays.
    
    ![Screenshot of the Salesforce login window displayed by Optimizely where users enter their Salesforce credentials to authenticate](/hc/article_attachments/44051235973645)
    

After you connect to Salesforce, the [Salesforce CRM connector tools](#h_01KJG46SGVDXEFEZPR6DQ0GW4R) become available in [Opal Chat](https://support.optimizely.com/hc/en-us/articles/36343492268813), [agents](https://support.optimizely.com/hc/en-us/articles/39407442255245), and [workflows](https://support.optimizely.com/hc/en-us/articles/39417564742797).

## Add instructions[](#h_01KJGAN94QY0GRB7S5KBXJKA8H)

Instructions help you control how Opal communicates with Salesforce based on how you use it. You should add at least one instruction before calling the [Salesforce CRM connector tools](#h_01KJG46SGVDXEFEZPR6DQ0GW4R).

As an example, follow the steps in the [Create instructions](https://support.optimizely.com/hc/en-us/articles/36553454584077-Manage-instructions#h_01KBNFD1CM9WP6HZ8W663VEJHV) documentation and enter the following information:

**Name** – _Salesforce Tools_

**Core Instruction**

**Salesforce Tool Usage Guidelines:** When interacting with Salesforce data, especially OpportunityOpportunity records, always adhere to the following rules:

1.  \*\*Opportunity Filtering:\*\*
    1.  When querying OpportunityOpportunity records, only include opportunities where type is one of the following:
        1.  New Customer - Single Product
        2.  New Customer - Multiple Products
        3.  Existing Customer - Cross Sell
        4.  Existing Customer - Cross Sell and Up Sell
    2.  If the user mentions "closed won opportunities" in the context of an Opportunity always use 'stage' of 'Closed Won - Finance'
    3.  If the user mentions "open opportunities" in the context of an Opportunity, filter by 'opportunity status' is 'Open'
    4.  If the user mentions "closed lost opportunities" in the context of an Opportunity always filter by 'stage' is 'Closed Lost'
    5.  If the user mentions "top opportunities" always sort descending by the \*\*RecurringSoftwareAmountChange\_\_c\*\* field
    6.  Always exclude opportunities with "test", "dummy", or "renewal" in the name (not case sensitive)
    7.  Always exclude opportunities where the \*\*RecurringSoftwareAmountChange\_\_c\*\* is null, a non-number, 0, or less than 1
2.  \*\*Opportunity Data:\*\*
    1.  When returning opportunity data always show: opportunity name, Recurring\_Software\_Amount\_Change\_\_c (label this field 'Recurring Software Amount (converted)'), owner, and close date at a minimum
    2.  Always use thousands separators (commas) when displaying number fields. Never show decimal points or cents.
    3.  \*\*IMPORTANT:\*\* If the user asks for opportunity "ARR", "amount", "revenue", or "value", always use the \*\*RecurringSoftwareAmountChange\_\_c\*\* field on the opportunity object because this is always in USD currency. Never use the 'Amount' field because it can be in different currencies.
3.  \*\*Salesperson/AE Mapping:\*\*
    1.  If the user mentions "salesperson" or "AE" in the context of an AountAount or OpportunityOpportunity, interpret this as a request for the "Primary Account Executive" field.
    2.  \*\*Implementation:\*\* When retrieving AountAount or OpportunityOpportunity records, include the Salesforce API field name for "Primary Account Executive" in the fieldsfields parameter (for example, PrimaryAccountExecutive\_\_cPrimaryAccountExecutive\_\_c or PrimaryAccountExecutivePrimaryAccountExecutive). \*Note: You may need to use\* sa≤orcecrmdescribeobjectsa≤orcecrmdescribeobject \*to confirm the exact API name of this field if it is a custom field.\*
4.  \*\*CSM Mapping:\*\*
    1.  If the user mentions "CSM" in the context of an AountAount or OpportunityOpportunity, interpret this as a request for the "Primary Customer Success Manager" field.
    2.  \*\*Implementation:\*\* When retrieving AountAount or OpportunityOpportunity records, include the Salesforce API field name for "Primary Customer Success Manager" in the fieldsfields parameter (for example, PrimaryCustomerSuccessManager\_\_cPrimaryCustomerSuccessManager\_\_c or PrimaryCustomerSuccessManagerPrimaryCustomerSuccessManager).
    3.  \*Note: You may need to use\* sa≤orcecrmdescribeobjectsa≤orcecrmdescribeobject \*to confirm the exact API name of this field if it is a custom field.\*

**When to use** – _When querying Salesforce data with Salesforce CRM tools._

Update the **Core Instruction** with additional information about how your organization uses Salesforce.

## Salesforce CRM connector tools[](#h_01KJG46SGVDXEFEZPR6DQ0GW4R)

After an Opal administrator [connects to Salesforce CRM](#h_01KJGAMXBZ63R87Z5P4WGBPA41) and [adds instructions](#h_01KJGAN94QY0GRB7S5KBXJKA8H) and you [authenticate with Salesforce CRM](#h_01KK01N9S5K4RP4WJ8DZQ43TJD), call the following tools in Opal. Click a tool's name to expand it and learn when to use the tool, required and optional parameters, and example prompts on how to call the tool. If you do not provide a required parameter, Opal prompts you for it.

### Objects[](#h_01KJG51D1DX01QA6PSH8C6TT7Z)

Use these tools to count, create, retrieve, and update standard and custom Salesforce records. Choose the tool that matches the operation you need to perform.

`salesforce_crm_count_object` – Counts records in any Salesforce object without retrieving the actual data.

*   **When to use**
    *   When you want to know the total count of objects without seeing the actual data.
    *   To check if records exist before performing operations.
    *   To verify data volumes efficiently.
*   **Parameters**
    *   `objectType` – Salesforce object type to count. For example, "Account", "Lead", or "Product\_Catalog\_\_c".
    *   (Optional) `filters` – Filter conditions as JSON string. For example, '{"Industry": "Technology"}'.
    *   (Optional) `createdAfter` – Filter records created on or after this date in YYYY-MM-DD format.
    *   (Optional) `createdBefore` – Filter records created on or before this date in YYYY-MM-DD format.
    *   (Optional) `customDateField` – Date or datetime field name to filter on, for instance "CloseDate".
    *   (Optional) `customDateAfter` – Filter records where `customDateField` is on or after this date in YYYY-MM-DD format.
    *   (Optional) `customDateBefore` – Filter records where `customDateField` is on or before this date in YYYY-MM-DD format.
*   **Example prompts**
    *   _How many accounts are there in Salesforce?_
    *   _Count the number of leads created this month._
    *   _How many opportunities are closing this quarter?_
    *   _Count cases that were closed last week._
    *   _How many active products are in the Product Catalog?_

`salesforce_crm_create_object` – Creates a new record in any Salesforce object.

*   **When to use**
    *   To create new records in Salesforce, such as Accounts, Leads, Contacts, Opportunities, or custom objects.
    *   When you need to add data to Salesforce programmatically.
    *   To streamline the creation of standard or custom Salesforce records.
*   **Parameters**
    *   `objectType` – Salesforce object type to create a record in. For example, "Account", "Lead", or "Product\_Catalog\_\_c".
    *   `fields` – Field values as a JSON string. For example, '{"Name": "Acme Corporation", "Industry": "Technology"}'.
*   **Example prompts**
    *   _Create a new Account named "Global Innovations" with Industry "Technology"._
    *   _I need to create a Lead for Jane Doe, company "Example Corp", email "jane.doe@example.com"._
    *   _Create an Opportunity named "Q2 2026 Expansion" with Stage "Prospecting" and CloseDate "2026-06-30"._
    *   _Add a new product to the Product Catalog with Name "Super Widget", SKU "SW-001", and Price 29.99._

`salesforce_crm_describe_object` – Describes a Salesforce object and gets its field metadata.

*   **When to use**
    *   To discover available fields for an object before creating or updating records.
    *   To check which fields are required, createable, or updateable.
    *   To get valid picklist values for picklist fields.
    *   To understand field types and their data formats.
*   **Parameters**
    *   `objectType` – Salesforce object type to describe. For example, "Account", "Lead", "Product\_Catalog\_\_c".
*   **Example prompts**
    *   _Describe the Account object in Salesforce._
    *   _Show me the fields available for the Lead object._
    *   _What are the metadata details for the custom object Product\_Catalog\_\_c?_

`salesforce_crm_get_object` – Retrieves a single record from any Salesforce object by ID or field search.

*   **When to use**
    *   To fetch details of a specific Salesforce record when you know its ID.
    *   To find a record by a unique field value, such as an email address or a custom SKU.
    *   To retrieve information about a single Account, Lead, Contact, Opportunity, or custom object record.
*   **Parameters**
    *   `objectType` – Salesforce object type to query. For example, "Account", "Lead", "Product\_Catalog\_\_c".
    *   (Optional) `recordId` – Salesforce record ID (18-character ID). If provided, `searchField` and `searchValue` are ignored.
    *   (Optional) `searchField` – Field name to search by, for instance, "Name", "Email", "SKU\_\_c". Required if `recordId` is not provided.
    *   (Optional) `searchValue` – Value to search for in the specified field. For example, "Acme"or "john@example.com". Required if `recordId` is not provided.
    *   (Optional) `fields` – Comma-separated list of specific field names to retrieve. For example, "Name,Email,Phone". If not specified, Opal returns all queryable fields.
*   **Example prompts**
    *   _Get the account details for ID "0015e000001ABC123"._
    *   _Find the lead with email "john@example.com"._
    *   _Retrieve the opportunity named "Q1 Deal"._
    *   _Show me the product details for SKU "PROD-12345"._

`salesforce_crm_list_object` – Lists records from any Salesforce object with optional filtering, sorting, and pagination.

*   **When to use**
    *   To search and retrieve multiple records from standard or custom Salesforce objects.
    *   To filter records by any field using advanced operators.
    *   To sort records by any field, including Amount, Name, CloseDate, or custom fields.
    *   To paginate through large result sets of Salesforce records.
*   **Parameters**
    *   `objectType` – Salesforce object type to query (for example, "Account", "Lead", "Opportunity").
    *   `fields` – Comma-separated list of specific field names to retrieve (for example, "Name,Email,Phone").
    *   (Optional) `filters` – Filter conditions as a JSON string.
    *   (Optional) `createdAfter` – Filter records created on or after this date in YYYY-MM-DD format.
    *   (Optional) `createdBefore` – Filter records created on or before this date in YYYY-MM-DD format.
    *   (Optional) `customDateField` – Date or datetime field name to filter on. For example, "CloseDate".
    *   (Optional) `customDateAfter` – Filter records where `customDateField` is on or after this date in YYYY-MM-DD format.
    *   (Optional) `customDateBefore` – Filter records where `customDateField` is on or before this date in YYYY-MM-DD format.
    *   (Optional) `sortBy` – Field name to sort results by. For example, "Amount" or "Name".
    *   (Optional) `sortOrder` – Sort order for results, "ASC" or "DESC".
    *   (Optional) `limit` – Maximum number of results to return. Default, 100.
    *   (Optional) `nextRecordsUrl` – Salesforce pagination URL from previous response.
*   **Example prompts**
    *   _List all accounts in the Technology industry, showing their Name, Industry, and Website._
    *   _Show me the top five opportunities by amount, including their Name, StageName, and Amount._
    *   _List leads created this month, displaying their Name, Email, and Company._
    *   _Find all cases with a "High" priority, showing CaseNumber, Subject, and Status._

`salesforce_crm_update_object` – Updates an existing record in any Salesforce object.

*   **When to use**
    *   To modify existing records in Salesforce, such as updating an Account's industry or a Lead's status.
    *   When you need to change specific fields of a Salesforce record.
    *   To automate updates to records based on new information or workflow changes.
*   **Parameters**
    *   `objectType` – Salesforce object type to update. For example, "Account", "Lead", "Product\_Catalog\_\_c".
    *   `recordId` – The ID of the record to update.
    *   `fields` – Field values to update as a JSON string. For example, '{"Industry": "Finance", "Phone": "555-9876"}'.
*   **Example prompts**
    *   _Update the Account with ID "0015e000001ABC123" to have Industry "Finance" and Phone "555-9876"._
    *   _Change the status of Lead "00Q5e000001XYZ789" to "Qualified"._
    *   _For Opportunity "0065e000001DEF456", set the StageName to "Closed Won" and Amount to 150000._
    *   _Update the Price\_\_c of Product\_Catalog\_\_c record "a005e000001ABC123" to 129.99._

### Custom objects[](#h_01KJG549ENYJSDB3VN1D4RA0PP)

Custom objects are data structures your organization has added to Salesforce beyond the standard set. Use these tools to discover which custom objects exist in your org and to query or filter records within them.

`salesforce_crm_list_custom_object_records` – Lists records from Salesforce custom objects with optional filtering and pagination.

*   **When to use**
    *   To search and retrieve multiple records from any Salesforce custom object.
    *   To filter custom object records by specific criteria, such as status or category.
    *   To sort custom object records by any field, including custom date or formula fields.
    *   To paginate through large sets of custom object records.
*   **Parameters**
    *   `objectName` – Custom object API name. Must end with `__c`. For example, "Product\_Catalog\_\_c".
    *   (Optional) `filters` – Filter conditions as a JSON string.
    *   (Optional) `createdAfter` – Filter records created on or after this date in YYYY-MM-DD format.
    *   (Optional) `createdBefore` – Filter records created on or before this date in YYYY-MM-DD format.
    *   (Optional) `customDateField` – Date or datetime field name to filter on. For example, "ExpirationDate\_\_c".
    *   (Optional) `customDateAfter` – Filter records where `customDateField` is on or after this date in YYYY-MM-DD format.
    *   (Optional) `customDateBefore` – Filter records where `customDateField` is on or before this date in YYYY-MM-DD format.
    *   (Optional) `sortBy` – Field name to sort results by. For example, "Name" or "Price\_\_c".
    *   (Optional) `sortOrder` – Sort order for results, "ASC" or "DESC".
    *   (Optional) `limit` – Maximum number of results to return. Default, 100.
    *   (Optional) `nextRecordsUrl` – Salesforce pagination URL from previous response.
*   **Example prompts**
    *   _List all records from the Product\_Catalog\_\_c custom object._
    *   _Show me active products in the Electronics category from Product\_Catalog\_\_c._
    *   _List all contracts from Contract\_\_c expiring in 2026._
    *   _Show me the top five most expensive products from Product\_Catalog\_\_c._

`salesforce_crm_list_custom_object_types` – Lists all custom object types in the Salesforce organization.

*   **When to use**
    *   To discover what custom objects exist in the Salesforce organization.
    *   To get the API names of custom objects needed for other operations.
    *   To understand the structure of custom data in Salesforce.
*   **Parameters**
    *   None
*   **Example prompts**
    *   _List all custom object types in Salesforce._
    *   _What custom objects are available in this Salesforce org?_
    *   _Show me the API names for all custom objects._

### Reports[](#h_01KJG54MX5KJ5PWKH9VSWC3WB9)

Use these tools to find, inspect, and run existing Salesforce reports. Start with the `salesforce_crm_list_reports` tool to discover available reports. Use the `salesforce_crm_describe_report` tool to review a report's structure and available filters before running it. Then use the `salesforce_crm_run_report` tool to retrieve the data.

`salesforce_crm_describe_report` – Retrieves metadata about a Salesforce report without executing it.

*   **When to use**
    *   Understand report structure before running it.
    *   See available columns and fields.
    *   Identify the filters you can apply.
    *   Understand groupings and aggregations.
*   **Parameters**
    *   `reportId` – Salesforce report ID to describe. Starts with "00O". For example, "00O5e000001ABC123". Use the `salesforce_crm_list_reports` tool to find available report IDs.
*   **Example prompts**
    *   _Tell me about Salesforce report "00O5e000001ABC123"._
    *   _What are the available columns and fields for Salesforce report "00O5e000001ABC123"._

`salesforce_crm_list_reports` – Retrieves a list of all reports accessible to you.

*   **When to use**
    *   Discover available reports.
    *   Find reports by name or folder.
    *   Identify report IDs for running or describing reports .
*   **Parameters**
    *   (Optional) `folderId` – ID to filter reports. Folder IDs start with "00l". For example, "00l5e000000ABC123".
        *   If provided, Opal returns only reports in this folder.
        *   If not provided, Opal returns all accessible reports.
*   **Example prompts**
    *   _List all reports._
    *   _List reports in a folderId: 00l5e000000ABC123**.**_

`salesforce_crm_run_report` – Runs a Salesforce report and returns the data.

*   **When to use**
    *   Execute an existing Salesforce report.
    *   Get report data with optional runtime filters.
    *   Retrieve aggregated and grouped data.
*   **Parameters**
    *   `reportId` – Salesforce report ID to execute. Starts with "00O". For example, "00O5e000001ABC123". Use the `salesforce_crm_list_reports` tool to find available report IDs.
    *   (Optional) `filters` – Filter conditions as a JSON string.
    *   (Optional) `includeDetails` – Whether to include detailed report results in the response. Default, true. Set to false for faster execution when you only need metadata.
*   **Example prompts**
    *   _Run a report without filters: { "reportId": "00O5e000001ABC123" }_
    *   _Run a report with runtime filters: { "reportId": "00O5e000001ABC123", "filters": "{\\"reportFilters\\": \[{\\"column\\": \\"CLOSE\_DATE\\", \\"operator\\": \\"greaterThan\\", ' + '\\"value\\": \\"2025-01-01\\"}\]}" }_
    *   _Run report without detailed results: { "reportId": "00O5e000001ABC123", "includeDetails": false }_ 

## Use cases[](#h_01KJG9V3D0BTTH780QCC1A2GZJ)

### Personalize content for new leads[](#h_01KJG9X3RF684XQ0M8KDJXWTMD)

**Challenge** – Marketing teams struggle to create and deliver personalized content to new leads, leading to generic outreach and lower engagement.

**Solution with Opal** – Opal can monitor Salesforce for newly created leads. Upon identifying a new lead, Opal automatically retrieves relevant details such as industry, company size, and expressed interests. Leveraging this data, Opal then drafts personalized marketing content, like a tailored email or a blog post summary, ready for review and immediate deployment by the marketing team. This ensures every new lead receives content that resonates, boosting engagement and qualification rates.

### Automate content suggestion for sales follow-up[](#h_01KJGA043Z96XYKDJ19M5M96X9)

**Challenge** – Sales representatives spend time searching for appropriate content (case studies, product sheets, or demos) to share with prospects at different stages of the sales cycle, often leading to delays and inconsistent messaging.

**Solution with Opal** – As opportunities advance through Salesforce stages, Opal proactively identifies the need for follow-up content. Based on the opportunity's details (for example, industry, specific product interest, or identified pain points), Opal searches your Content Marketing Platform (CMP) for the most relevant assets. It then suggests these assets directly to the sales rep or even drafts a personalized email incorporating the content, streamlining the follow-up process and ensuring timely, relevant communication.

### Streamline opportunity reporting[](#h_01KJGA0DJMCMKW4GW5ATY6JR0Z)

**Challenge** – Business users need quick, up-to-date insights into sales pipeline health and opportunity status, but compiling reports from Salesforce can be time-consuming and require specific expertise.

**Solution with Opal** – Ask Opal for a summary of open opportunities, top deals, or opportunities by stage. Opal queries Salesforce in real-time, aggregates the data, and presents it in an easily digestible format, such as a dynamic table or chart within an Opal canvas. This eliminates manual reporting efforts, providing instant, actionable insights for sales leaders and executives, unifying reporting into a single, accessible interface.

### Proactive engagement for at-risk opportunities[](#h_01KJGA0TQ46DVDCVJPZPWQTA30)

**Challenge** – Sales teams often react to at-risk opportunities rather than proactively addressing potential issues, leading to lost deals. Identifying these opportunities early and knowing the best course of action is critical.

**Solution with Opal** – Opal continuously monitors Salesforce opportunities for signs of risk, such as prolonged inactivity, approaching close dates without recent engagement, or changes in competitor presence. When an at-risk opportunity is detected, Opal alerts the sales representative and suggests next-best actions. This could include drafting a re-engagement email, recommending a specific piece of content to share, or prompting a call with a key stakeholder, letting you proactively intervene to keep deals on track.

### Competitive intelligence for sales pitches[](#h_01KJGA14177VE19FEX0GQCE4SE)

**Challenge** – Sales representatives need quick access to up-to-date competitive intelligence to effectively position Optimizely's solutions during critical sales pitches, but this information is often scattered or difficult to retrieve on demand.

**Solution with Opal** – When a sales rep is preparing for a pitch, they can ask Opal for competitive intelligence related to a specific opportunity. Opal retrieves any competitor information stored in Salesforce for that opportunity and then leverages its extensive internal knowledge base (including up-to-date competitor analysis) to provide key differentiators, battle cards, and strategic talking points against the identified competitors. This empowers sales teams with instant, relevant insights to strengthen their pitches and close more deals.
